_comment: Seven beats. Every figure in here is measured and every one has a file, a run URL or a command behind it in the repository. captionText carries the exact spelling a judge will check. speechText carries the form a voice engine pronounces correctly. Nothing is rounded up and nothing is claimed that the code cannot reach.

segments._beat: The problem in the buyer's words, and the measured base rate. No market, one named role.
segments.captionText: Once a year an engineering director signs that the security checks are in place. At the last audit he was asked to prove it for one repository. All he had was a green tick. Across 120 public repositories, 21 of the 47 that run their own security script have it narrower than the step's name claims.
segments.speechText: Once a year, an engineering director signs a statement that the security checks are in place. At the last audit, he was asked to prove it for one repository. All he had was a green tick. We measured 120 public repositories, none of them ours. Of the 47 that run their own security script, 21 have it narrower than the step's name claims.

segments._beat: The refutation. A real green run on a commit built to break the rule.
segments.captionText: This is a real GitHub Actions run. It reports success on commit 9762a80, which carries a file the pipeline's own scan detects. The log reads: planted finding detected, this build must not pass. The step exited 1. The job is green.

segments._beat: The second lie, and it was not in the design. Found by reading the API back.
segments.captionText: There is a second lie in that run, and it is the sharper one. The forge reports the scan step itself as success. continue-on-error rewrites the step's own conclusion, so the badge, the job and the API all agree. Only the log disagrees. A dashboard built on step conclusions calls this pipeline healthy.
